LESSON: FICTION AND NON- FICTION 1.3.1 FICTION: NOVEL FROM KENYA

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: LITERATURE IN ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.3: Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya, part of Strand 1 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How do novels promote cultural awareness in a country? 2. Why are novels significant in literature?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. team up with peers to search for features of prose fiction from online and offline sources. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. team up with peers to search for features of prose fiction from online and offline sources. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body, use adapted 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non- Fiction 1.3.1 Fiction: Novel from Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: This is nurtured as the learner reads clearly and engages with peers when conducting a

reader’s theatre to read the set novel from Kenya.

● Self- efficacy: This is enhanced as the learner exhibits self-confidence when relating the cultural aspects in the novel to

real life.

Values:
● Respect: This is inculcated as the learner appreciates the contributions of the others during discussions and peer review.

● Unity: This is enhanced as the learner collaborates with others to team up to prepare a flow chart showing the

chronological order of events in the novel from Kenya and displays in class.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Citizenship: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with information by reading a novel from Kenya and relating events to

real life.
